variables.name: LiquidTimeConstant
variables.mechanism: Learnable time constants in liquid networks modulate the membrane potential decay rate, enabling continuous-time dynamic adaptation to non-stationary temporal data.

variables.name: SpikingEventDriven
variables.mechanism: Event-driven spiking mechanism generates sparse pulses only when the membrane potential crosses a threshold, reducing energy consumption and providing nonlinear event triggers.

variables.name: OnlineAdaptiveLearning
variables.mechanism: The combined liquid-gated membrane dynamics and sparse spiking enable online adaptation to non-stationary time series with low energy cost.

variables.name: EnergyConsumption
variables.mechanism: Sparse event-driven spiking reduces the number of operations, leading to lower energy consumption compared to dense SNNs.

variables.name: TaskComplexity
variables.mechanism: Task complexity simultaneously influences the need for liquid time constants and spiking sparsity (cause) and the achievable online adaptation performance and energy consumption (effect).

variables.name: HardwarePlatform
variables.mechanism: The hardware platform (e.g., neuromorphic vs. GPU) simultaneously affects the feasibility of implementing liquid time constants and spiking mechanisms (cause) and the measured energy consumption and adaptation speed (effect).

counterfactual.question: If the liquid time constant mechanism were removed (i.e., fixed decay rates), would the network still achieve low-energy online adaptation to non-stationary time series?
counterfactual.predicted_answer: Without liquid time constants, the network would lose its continuous-time adaptive gating, likely reducing online adaptation performance on non-stationary data. Energy consumption might remain low due to spiking sparsity, but the ability to dynamically adjust membrane potentials would be compromised, leading to worse task performance.

alternative_explanations: The observed benefits may stem from the universal approximation property of liquid networks alone, independent of spiking mechanisms.
Energy savings could be primarily due to hardware-specific optimizations rather than the spiking event-driven mechanism.
Chemical reaction networks might outperform both liquid networks and SNNs on certain tasks, as suggested by opposing evidence.
graphs.hypothesis_text: 結合 Liquid Networks 的動態時間常數與 Spiking Neural Networks 的事件驅動機制，可設計一種新型神經網路，其神經元在連續時間內以液態閘控方式調整膜電位，並僅在閾值跨越時產生稀疏脈衝，從而實現對非平穩時序資料的線上適應學習，且能耗遠低於現有 SNN。
